title: Bug: hosting an agent with a pubsub config fails when broadcast topic is not configured
body:
## Description

When an agent is configured with an `AgentPubSubConfig` and `broadcast_topic` is omitted, hosting the agent through any runner entrypoint that wires pub/sub routes (`register_routes`, `subscribe`, `serve`) leads to the following error:
```
ValueError: AgentPubSubConfig missing topic for broadcast handler on_broadcast
```

## Steps to Reproduce

Using the Drasi change-driven example on my `drasi-trigger-broadcast-bug` branch
https://github.com/JeffreyJPZ/dapr-agents/tree/drasi-trigger-broadcast-bug/examples/ext-drasi-change-driven-agents-k8s

## Expected Behavior

Hosting an agent should not result in any error as `broadcast_topic` is optional.

In `DurableAgent.register_workflows`, the broadcast workflow is (correctly) not registered with the workflow runtime when the broadcast topic is omitted:
```python
if self.broadcast_topic_name:
      runtime.register_workflow(
          self._named(self.on_broadcast, self.broadcast_workflow_name)
      )
```

Similarly, broadcast subscriptions should not be wired when the broadcast topic is omitted.

## Cause

`on_broadcast` is decorated with `broadcast=True`:
```python
@message_router(message_model=BroadcastMessage, broadcast=True)
def on_broadcast(self, ctx: wf.DaprWorkflowContext, message: dict):
    ...
```

When the agent is hosted, `AgentRunner._wire_pubsub_routes` then discovers all decorated handlers including `on_broadcast`:
```python
def _build_pubsub_specs(
        self, agent: DurableAgent, config: Any
    ) -> list[PubSubRouteSpec]:
        handlers = get_decorated_methods(agent, "_is_message_handler")        
        ...
        for _, handler in handlers.items():
            meta = getattr(handler, "_message_router_data", {})
            is_broadcast = meta.get("is_broadcast", False)
            topic: Optional[str] = (
                config.broadcast_topic if is_broadcast else config.agent_topic
            )
            if not topic:
                kind = "broadcast" if is_broadcast else "direct"
                raise ValueError(
                    f"AgentPubSubConfig missing topic for {kind} handler {handler.__name__}"
                )
            ...
        ...
```

When it tries to handle `on_broadcast`, `is_broadcast` is always `True`, which causes `topic` to be `None` as no broadcast topic exists. This results in the error described above.

## Suggested Fix

Instead of throwing, add a guard that skips broadcast handlers if no broadcast topic is configured.

Ideally there should also be a regression test, but I think tests for `AgentRunner` are generally lacking so it might be a lot of work to set up.

linked_prs.title: fix: skip broadcast handlers if no broadcast topic is configured
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/dapr_agents/workflow/runners/agent.py b/dapr_agents/workflow/runners/agent.py
index 383efd507..670920050 100644
--- a/dapr_agents/workflow/runners/agent.py
+++ b/dapr_agents/workflow/runners/agent.py
@@ -364,9 +364,16 @@ def _build_pubsub_specs(
                 config.broadcast_topic if is_broadcast else config.agent_topic
             )
             if not topic:
-                kind = "broadcast" if is_broadcast else "direct"
+                if is_broadcast:
+                    # Skip broadcast handlers if the agent has no broadcast topic configured,
+                    # as no registered broadcast workflow exists to handle messages.
+                    logger.debug(
+                        f"[{self._name}] Agent {getattr(agent, 'name', agent)} has no broadcast topic; "
+                        f"skipping broadcast handler {handler.__name__}."
+                    )
+                    continue
                 raise ValueError(
-                    f"AgentPubSubConfig missing topic for {kind} handler {handler.__name__}"
+                    f"AgentPubSubConfig missing agent topic for handler {handler.__name__}"
                 )
 
             schemas = meta.get("message_schemas") or []
